Finally, astrophysical sources yield extreme fluxes: cosmogenic neutrinos are produced at ultra-high energies (PeV to EeV) when cosmic rays interact with the Cosmic Microwave Background via the GZK effect, while extragalactic neutrinos (TeV to PeV) originate from high-energy cosmic accelerators such as Active Galactic Nuclei, blazars, and Gamma-Ray Bursts beyond the Milky Way[cite: 1].
